Chemistry

Radboud University

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

Radboud Chemistry studies how molecular structure determines properties and reactions. Its programme combines synthetic, analytical, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry with mathematics, physics, extensive laboratory training and an individual research internship.

UCR offers genuine biochemistry, molecular biology, laboratory work, environmental geochemistry and quantitative methods. These contributions do not build the sustained chemical theory, synthesis and measurement at the centre of this degree. We therefore show Radboud’s curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a sufficiently close alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Ordinary full-time Chemistry bachelor; 36 EC all-BC1 example

The 180 EC comprises 126 EC of required courses, 36 EC of conditioned scientific choice, a 12 EC individual research internship and 6 EC of free choice. The displayed choice is one permitted BC1 example, not a set of universally required courses; options may not run every year. Internship entry requires 120 EC including all first-year courses and prior proposal approval. First-year Academic Skills carries no extra credits; RADAr participation is required, but a passing score is not. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 39 EC. Course entry, attendance, overlap and approval rules apply.
